ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed directors, shareholders, beneficial owners (threshold ≥ 25%), and financially-significant individuals must undergo mandatory screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Australian DFAT Consolidated List, and Samoa domestic sanctions/designation list. PEP identification (politically exposed persons, including family members and close associates) is mandatory, with enhanced due diligence (EDD) applied where a PEP is identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SIFA International Companies Registry (via Samoa International Finance Authority eServices portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script (English/Samoan alphabet). Chinese or non-Latin script names may be used ONLY as an unofficial translation and do not appear on the registry certificate. Names must end with a recognised limited-liability suffix (e.g., 'Limited', 'Ltd.', 'International Company', 'IC') and must not misleadingly resemble an existing domestic or international company.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or licensed agent may submit a written administrative appeal to the Registrar of International Companies within 21 calendar days from the date of rejection. The appeal must cite the proposed name, the exact rejection ground, and legal argument demonstrating compliance. Where a sensitive token is involved, prior written clearance from the relevant sectoral regulator (e.g., Central Bank of Samoa for 'Bank'; Ministry of Health for 'Medical' under licensing statutes) must be appended. The SIFA Appeals Committee will issue a final determination within 14 business days; further judicial review is available in the Supreme Court of Samoa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements through a licensed registered agent in Samoa are permissible for an International Company engaged purely in offshore medical-device export, provided the registered agent maintains a physical registered office address in Samoa. A separate physical operational office in Samoa is not required for this industry, but the company must maintain adequate substance documentation (directors, registered agent, financial records) to demonstrate commercial substance if challenged.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated low-to-moderate risk of approximately 10% for an unannounced physical inspection during the first year of operation, given the export-only business model and low-risk AML tier. The risk increases if adverse media, PEP association, or inconsistent UBO disclosure arises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), sections 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15 and 18; Companies Act 2001 for domestic ancillary matters; International Companies Rules 1988; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Regulations 2018.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (Form IC-1) together with Memorandum and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; an International Company may be incorporated with zero paid-up capital. Share capital is determined by the Memorandum and Articles. No escrow account is required under Samoan law for incorporation capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers and directors of the Company do hereby approve the subscription and allotment of shares as recorded in the register of members. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company shall be located at the office of the registered agent in Apia, Samoa. FURTHER RESOLVED that the following persons are appointed as officers with full authority to execute banking documents and contracts: Managing Director, Secretary and Compliance Officer. FURTHER RESOLVED that the corporate seal is adopted and the registered agent is retained. FURTHER RESOLVED that the directors are authorized to open bank accounts, complete all statutory filings, obtain operating licenses, and take all lawful actions necessary to attain full corporate and operational standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage a SIFA-licensed Registered Agent and Reserve Company Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a professional services agreement with a SIFA-licensed registered agent. Instruct the agent to submit a name reservation request to SIFA using Form IR-4. Include the intended company name and consent from the director. SIFA will issue a name clearance confirming that the proposed name is not identical to any existing company in Samoa.
required_dossiers: Due diligence documents on beneficial owners (proof of identity and address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a new name reservation with distinguishing words or a different suffix; request a written reason and re-file within five working days free of additional nomination fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Constitutional Documents and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association with the assistance of the registered agent. The charter must include a standard objects clause authorizing medical device manufacturing and international trade. Have the subscribers sign the documents before a notary public. Prepare the register of directors, shareholders, officers and registered charges.
required_dossiers: Signed consent to act as director and officer
Letter of authorization to registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA or agent determines that the objects clause requires clarification, amend the clause via board resolution and re-notarize. No additional government fee for amendment prior to filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Incorporation (IC-1) with SIFA through the registered agent. Attach the notarized Memorandum and Articles, name clearance, and declarations of solvency and non-resident ownership. The Registrar verifies compliance with the International Companies Act and International Companies Rules.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA issues a query or requisition, the agent must submit a written response within 14 days. Correct the stated defect and re-file with the Registrar; if the application is rejected, appeal in writing to the Minister for Commerce within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay Government Fees and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon SIFA's approval, pay the state incorporation fee (currently USD 250 or equivalent in Samoan tala) and the annual registration fee. SIFA issues the Certificate of Incorporation and any additional certified copies upon request.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed, issue a written request for expedited issuance to the Registrar, invoking the statutory service standard. Follow up through the SIFA helpline and receive certificate confirmation within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt First Board Resolution and Appoint Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board of Directors and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting in accordance with Articles. Record minutes adopting the pro-forma first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office address, appointment of officers and adoption of corporate seal. Execute the minutes and distribute executed copies to the registered agent and SIFA where requested.
required_dossiers: Draft minutes of the first board meeting
Consent forms from directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any unanimous consent resolution is challenged by a shareholder, hold a physical or virtual board meeting and re-vote. Amendments to officer appointments must be notified to the registered agent for corporate records and to SIFA if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Beneficial Ownership Register and AML Compliance Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA AML Unit through the Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a confidential beneficial ownership return to SIFA in compliance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Regulations 2018. The return must identify all individuals with significant control and provide source of funds declarations for the ultrasound console manufacturing operations.
required_dossiers: Copy of passport and proof of address for each ultimate beneficial owner
Corporate chart for fully owned subsidiaries (if none, nil declaration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA rejects or queries the beneficial ownership declaration, provide supplemental evidence within 10 business days, including bank references or certified documentation. Non-compliance is cured by submitting a revised return and paying a modest administrative amendment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Medical Device Manufacturing Licence and Industrial Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Health (Health Regulatory Sciences) and Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Ministry of Health for a Manufacturer's Licence for Medical Devices covering the phased-array color Doppler ultrasound console production line. Submit technical files, manufacturing process flow, quality management documentation, and proposed labeling. Simultaneously file an Environmental Impact Assessment application with MNRE and obtain fire safety pre-approval from FESA.
required_dossiers: Quality management system certificate (ISO 13485 or equivalent registration plan)
Technical dossier under IMDRF format for diagnostic device
Site layout and industrial facility description
Fire safety system description and floor plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOH requires additional evidence, submit a supplementary technical response within 15 working days. For EIA, publish the draft environmental management plan if required; for FESA, correct any fire safety gaps in the physical facility and schedule a re-inspection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil Defence, Occupational Clearance and Commencement of Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) and Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour Labour Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange physical inspection of the manufacturing premises to obtain the Fire Safety Certificate and Occupational Health and Safety compliance statement. Confirm that the plant has passed structural load inspection for installation of the imaging assembly equipment. Receive final license copies and maintain a regulatory compliance register for annual renewals.
required_dossiers: Occupational Health and Safety clearance form
Certificate of incorporation and business licence evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection identifies non-compliance, implement corrective works within two weeks and request a re-inspection. If OHS clearance is withheld, submit a corrective action plan to MCIL and obtain conditional approval to begin low-risk administrative work while rectifying flags.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health (Health Regulatory Sciences Division) in conjunction with Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour investment and manufacturing licensing unit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Manufacturer's Licence for Medical Devices (Portable Diagnostic Imaging Equipment) under the Health Ordinance 1959 and the Samoa Medical Devices Regulations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) — Environmental Assessment and Monitoring Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Report required for manufacturing operation generating process effluent and electronic waste.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet National Water Quality Standards and WHO guideline values for industrial effluents; airborne volatile organic compounds (VOCs) limited to 50 mg/m3 with engineering controls; hazardous electronic waste shall be segregated and exported under the Waste Management Act 2011 and Basel Convention guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) confirming compliance with premises fire suppression and escape routes; structural load inspection and certification for installation of medical imaging assembly lines; Occupational Health and Safety clearance from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour Labour Division guaranteeing workplace noise, ventilation and ionizing radiation safety protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue, Government of Samoa (Samoa Revenue Authority / Inland Revenue and Customs administration); official taxpayer portal and e-services: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC) is first incorporated through a licensed registered agent with the Samoa International Finance Authority / Registrar of International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended). Because the IC is structured as a non-resident tax-exempt offshore entity, it is not automatically registered with the Samoa Ministry for Revenue and is generally not required to obtain a domestic taxpayer identification number or file income tax returns for foreign-source income. If the IC intends to conduct any taxable activity in Samoa, import medical-device components, employ local staff, or claim zero-rating/refund of Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) on export sales, it must apply to the Ministry for Revenue for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and obtain separate VAGST registration. The application requires submission of the IC certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles, registered-agent certificate, directors and beneficial-owner identity evidence, a local business licence if applicable, and the value of expected annual taxable supplies. The Ministry then issues the TIN and, upon meeting the registration threshold or applying voluntarily, a VAGST registration number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or US-style entity classification election exists under Samoa law. A Samoa International Company is automatically tax-exempt on all offshore income by statute and is not a pass-through entity for Samoan income-tax purposes; the exemption applies unless the IC converts to a domestic company under the Companies Act or exercises a permitted local business activity. The IC may voluntarily register for VAGST even below the statutory turnover threshold in order to zero-rate exports and recover input tax, and may apply to the Ministry for Revenue for a binding ruling or private clearance on the export zero-rating eligibility of medical-imaging supplies. No hybrid-mismatch elections or dual-residency tax elections are available in the Samoa domestic regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 taxable annual turnover in Samoan Tālā (compulsory registration); voluntary registration permitted for exporters, with the threshold measured over any consecutive 12-month period
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not currently mandate real-time electronic fiscal invoicing, government API clearance, or digital stamping for commercial invoices. A VAGST-registered exporter must issue a compliant VAGST tax invoice in paper or PDF format containing prescribed particulars within 28 days of the supply. Export clearance is handled through the Customs Division using the ASYCUDA World electronic customs management system, which requires an approved electronic export declaration before the Color Doppler Ultrasound Console consignment is loaded. The Ministry for Revenue provides an e-filing portal for VAGST returns and tax payments, but that portal is not an invoice-clearance or e-invoicing fiscal gateway.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the export sale of goods if the goods are supplied to a person who is outside Samoa, are physically exported from Samoa within the statutory period and are not subsequently re-imported for local use, and the exporter retains sufficient evidence of the international supply chain. Zero-rating also covers certain services supplied directly to a non-resident recipient and consumed entirely outside Samoa, including installation, testing, calibration and software support associated with an exported medical-imaging console, provided the services are not performed for a Samoa-resident benefit. The Color Doppler Ultrasound Console must be sold under an export contract, consigned to a foreign hospital or distributor, and cleared by Samoa Customs under the export declaration; mere local delivery to a related party will not qualify. Input VAT incurred on local purchase of components, consumables, calibration equipment and freight services is recoverable against the zero-rated export output; any input tax attributable to domestic taxable supplies remains creditable only to the extent of the VAGST return and invoice-substantiation requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World electronic CusDec clearance record)
Commercial Invoice issued by the Samoa International Company to the overseas buyer
Packing List identifying the ultrasound console, serial number, HS classification 9018.13 and export quantity
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the goods from Samoa
Certificate of Origin or manufacturer's compliance certificate if required by the importing jurisdiction
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice evidencing receipt of the foreign-currency sales proceeds from the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Samoa Revenue Authority may subject export zero-rating claims to desk or field audit, document verification through ASYCUDA Customs records, bank-inward-remittance reconciliation, and inspection of warehouse/logistics records. If the exporter fails to produce the complete export documentation bundle, fails to prove shipment from Samoa, or fails to bring the export proceeds into the country within the 180-day statutory repatriation window without a Ministry-approved foreign-exchange waiver, the zero-rated treatment is retrospectively reversed and the full 15% VAGST becomes payable together with late-payment interest and penalties. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims, false Customs declarations, forged bills of lading, artificial round-tripping of goods, or misstatement of the destination or buyer attract additional civil shortfall penalties of up to the amount of tax evaded, prosecution under the Tax Administration Act and Customs law, fines, imprisonment of responsible directors/off-icers, and cancellation or suspension of the International Company's registration by the Registrar of International Companies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) – Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa, acting under the Exchange Control Act 1970, the Financial Institutions Act 1996, and the CBS Exchange Control Guidelines
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is convertible for current-account trade settlements through authorized dealers; capital-account transactions require prior CBS approval or exemption. International Companies in Samoa operate in the Tax-Exempt Zone and have no Samoan income-tax or withholding-tax on profit remittances. However, dividends, loan repayments, liquidation proceeds, and other capital-related remittances must be supported by audited financial statements and submitted through a licensed commercial bank. The CBS monitors cross-border flows under its exchange control mandate, and non-resident owners must demonstrate source of funds upon capital injection. The practical remittance hurdle is not taxation but documentary compliance with CBS forms, BO registers, and compliance with anti-money-laundering requirements of the banking channel.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoa requires all export proceeds to be repatriated to an authorized dealer within six months from the date of export shipment. Unless a foreign-currency account retention exemption is granted by the CBS under the Exchange Control Act, 100% of export receipts must be offered for conversion into WST through an authorized dealer within one month of receipt. For International Companies that operate as offshore export vehicles, the CBS may permit foreign-currency retention where the proceeds are contractually committed to foreign-currency trade liabilities; any net surplus not so committed must be surrendered. All export documents, customs declarations, bills of lading, and commercial invoices must be retained for five years and presented upon CBS inspection.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Samoa does not maintain an electronic-money institution (EMI) licensing regime. Non-bank digital EMI providers are not authorized to conduct foreign-exchange clearing or hold client funds unless separately licensed as banks under the Financial Institutions Act 1996. Offshore digital EMIs cannot settle WST transactions or access Samoa's domestic interbank clearing infrastructure without a licensed bank partner. An International Company should therefore use a tier-1 Samoan commercial bank or a reputable global banking provider with a Samoa-located branch.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement exists for directors to appear physically before a Samoan bank. CBS AML/CFT rules permit non-face-to-face account opening where the International Company's beneficial owners are identified through certified copies of passports, apostilled corporate documents, and a registered-agent attestation. The bank will normally require a video-conference interview for directors or ultimate beneficial owners, especially for offshore structures with trust layers. High-risk jurisdictions trigger enhanced due diligence and may require documents to be certified by a recognized notary public or a Samoan consular officer. A local licensed international company agent is strongly advised to coordinate onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer shares or blank-transfer instruments discovered in the International Company constitutional documents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of the register of shareholders demonstrating mandatory surrender or cancellation of all bearer shares; a board resolution confirming no bearer instruments remain in circulation; a legal opinion from Samoan counsel confirming compliance with the International Companies Act; current beneficial ownership register filed with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ultimate beneficial ownership due to layered discretionary trusts and nominee directors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled trust deed, deed of indemnity, and letter of consent from the licensed trustee; SIFA-beneficial-ownership extracts showing each natural person with ownership or control; a signed BO declaration in the bank-prescribed format; organizational chart tracing the economic interest from trust beneficiaries to the color Doppler ultrasound console business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade counterparty or transaction exhibits sanctions, PEP, or adverse media links
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBS and international sanctions screening summary from the correspondent bank; PEP self-certification for each beneficial owner; transaction-flow document with underlying supply contracts and shipping documents; bank statements or invoices demonstrating arm's-length commercial dealing; adverse-media review prepared by a compliance advisory firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medical device industry license not presented at account opening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the Samoa Ministry of Health import/export authorization or mutual-recognition license for the medical diagnostic scanner; evidence of regulatory licensure in the destination jurisdiction (e.g., FDA 510(k), CE marking, or TGA), if applicable; product technical file and liability insurance certificate; confirmation from the Ministry of Commerce that no additional export embargo applies.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections and shareholder loans must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the beneficial owner's bank to the International Company's designated WST or USD account at a Samoan authorized dealer. The wire must state the CBS-approved transaction purpose code — 'EM1 Equity Capital Direct Investment' for shares or 'EL1 Direct Investment Loans' for shareholder borrowings, or the corresponding Samoan exchange-control nomenclature. Documentation includes: board resolution approving the capital injection, executed subscription agreement or loan agreement, proof of source of wealth, CBS exchange-control notification form where applicable, and a SIFA beneficial ownership declaration. Funds will be credited only after the receiving bank completes inbound funds verification and confirms the capital-account classification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails for outbound trade settlements are SWIFT MT103 'Our' or 'Cover' payments for TT wire transfers and irrevocable commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 via SWIFT MT700/MT710. Where a supplier requires an LC, the Samoan issuing bank opens the credit through its correspondent bank and settles via SWIFT MT756/MT202 when documents conform under the LC. For export collections, SWIFT MT400 or MT410 may be used through the CBCA network. All outbound trade payments require invoicing in USD, AUD, NZD, or EUR when the bank cannot settle WST; the bank will verify the underlying purchase order, commercial invoice, cargo documents, and CBS form for the specific trade. No alternative domestic clearing system exists for foreign-currency trade payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable forwards with a licensed Samoan authorized dealer for genuine trade and balance-sheet exposure
Cross-currency swaps executed with a licensed bank for long-dated USD/AUD/NZD liability hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only as an offshore mirror hedge for WST-denominated obligations, with CBS notification and proof of economic exposure
Foreign-currency options when used to hedge committed trade flows under a confirmed banking facility
Natural hedging through structured foreign-currency accounts and multi-currency pooling where approved by the CBS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) / Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On each anniversary of incorporation, with no statutory grace period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of USD 100 plus 10% per month on the outstanding fee; continued non-payment for 3 months triggers automatic administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing required no later than 15 days before each anniversary of incorporation, accompanied by proof of current registered agent and office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of USD 75; failure to file within 30 days of the due date may lead to an automatic strike-off and loss of legal personality

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Declaration of Beneficial Ownership Records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed registered agent (filed with SIFA under anti-money-laundering obligations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the anniversary of incorporation, or upon any change in shareholding / beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with beneficial ownership record confirmation may expose the registered agent to AML penalties and may cause the entity's name to be reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit under the International Companies Act 1987 for a standard International Company, unless the entity is listed on a securities exchange, or the shareholders by special resolution elect to appoint an auditor
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or acceptable local GAAP if financial statements are voluntarily prepared; statutory record-keeping requires accounting records sufficient to disclose the company's financial position with reasonable accuracy

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Samoa maintains no public beneficial-ownership register; the International Company must confirm current beneficial ownership details to its licensed registered agent annually and within 21 days of any shareholding transfer or material change

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 (statutorily exempt); USD 3,000 - 7,500 if an unconditional audit is voluntarily procured

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% on all assessable income for an International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption from corporate income tax, capital gains tax, withholding tax, stamp duty, gift duty, and all other taxes, rates, duties, and levies on income, operations, shares, dividends, and distributions. Only an annual government license fee (approximately WST 250–1,000 depending on authorized capital) and registration/agent fees apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return (Form CIT-10) is required for an International Company because of its exempt status; instead, an Annual Return (Form IC-AR/Exempt Declaration) must be lodged with the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour / Samoa International Companies Registry via the online eRegistry portal (www.registry.gov.ws).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Return and declaration of continued exemption must be filed within one month (30 days) after the anniversary of the date of incorporation or the date of issuance of the international company license, whichever is earlier.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full registered name of the International Company, including all punctuation and language characters
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors or shareholders must enter the name as recorded in the Certificate of Incorporation; transliterated Latin characters acceptable if no English version exists.
Enter the unique number issued by the Samoa Registrar of International Companies; do not use any domestic company registration number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in Samoa (street, PO Box, electronic agent email)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be a physical or licensed agent address in Samoa; a PO Box alone is insufficient; the address must match the agent's registered details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and address of the licensed registered agent (e.g., local trust company or corporate services provider)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the IC operates through a non-resident trust or management company using a Samoan agent, the agent's licensed identifier must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of directors, beneficial owners, and shareholders with percentage of ownership and nationalities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial ownership is permitted without prior approval; however, fully transparent beneficial ownership information must be maintained and filed for AML/CFT purposes. Samoa does not permit bearer shares for new ICs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of continued tax-exempt status and statement that the company has not undertaken any domestically prohibited commercial activity (e.g., doing business with Samoan residents inside Samoa)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the IC leases mobile color Doppler ultrasound consoles to Samoan hospitals or clinics, it will lose automatic tax exemption and must immediately register under the ordinary Companies Act 2001 and Income Tax Act 2015.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual fee computation schedule (authorized capital bands) and proof of payment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be remitted by wire transfer to Samoa International Companies Registry account; non-resident payers should include the registry reference number to avoid misallocation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Annual Return attracts a penalty of WST 20–100 per day of delay plus an administrative strike-off after 90 days. Continued non-compliance results in automatic dissolution/removal from the registry, a WST 1,000 restoration fee, and the personal liability of directors and beneficial owners for all debts and obligations incurred during the period of non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends, distributions, and liquidation proceeds paid by a Samoan International Company to any non-resident shareholder; the law expressly prohibits any withholding or other tax on shareholder distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Since the statutory dividend withholding tax is already 0%, no application for treaty relief is generally needed. If, exceptionally, the IC elects to be treated as an ordinary Samoan company (e.g., because it is carrying on a domestic business), then treaty relief under a Samoa DTA (e.g., Australia, New Zealand, Norway, Sweden) requires: (1) submission of a Tax Residency Certificate (Form TRC-1) issued by Samoa Ministry of Revenue; (2) submission of the counterparty jurisdiction's TRC to Samoa Inland Revenue; (3) filing of Form DTA-A2 no later than 21 days before the dividend payment; and (4) a beneficial ownership declaration stating the ultimate recipient has economic substance outside Samoa and is not a conduit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For an International Company: 0% on royalties and interest paid to non-residents. For an ordinary resident Samoan company under the Income Tax Act 2015: 15% statutory on royalty and 15% on interest paid to non-residents, reduced under DTAs to 5–10% (interest/royalty) depending on treaty partner (e.g., Australia 0% on interest? Not applicable to an IC). Royalties for medical software and non-tangible ultrasound technology embedded in color Doppler consoles paid by an IC to a foreign affiliate remain fully exempt; the IC should obtain an exemption confirmation letter from the Samoan Ministry of Revenue when banks require documentary validation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Nil / Not Applicable for a tax-exempt International Company. Because the IC has a 0% corporate tax rate, Samoa's transfer pricing documentation thresholds (Mandatory Country-by-Country Report threshold of WST 500,000,000 and Local File/Master File threshold of WST 5,000,000) do not apply. However, if the IC enters into transactions with a Samoan resident entity or a treaty-protected ordinary company, contemporaneous documentation must still be prepared to prove arm's length pricing in case the IC is re-characterized as a resident taxpayer.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's International Companies (Economic Substance) Amendment Act 2018/2020 applies to ICs conducting 'relevant activities' — namely banking, insurance, shipping, distribution, service center, finance/leasing, headquarters, fund management, and intellectual property holding. Manufacturing of medical diagnostic scanners and the export of color Doppler ultrasound consoles, if conducted through a Samoan entity with physical operations elsewhere, is generally NOT a 'pure equity holding' or IP-only activity; nevertheless, a 3% minimum economic substance test may apply. The IC must demonstrate: (a) actual management and control in Samoa; (b) adequate physical presence (staff, premises, export logistics); and (c) core income-generating activities performed in Samoa. If the IC is a pure holding company for the medical equipment IP, it qualifies for the reduced substance test and must maintain: registered office, Samoan-resident director, and minutes of board meetings held in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Loss of International Company Exempt Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Carrying on any trade, business, or activity inside Samoa with a Samoan resident without prior government permission, or deriving income from the supply or installation of color Doppler ultrasound consoles to Samoan hospitals, clinics, or the Samoa Ministry of Health without converting the IC to an ordinary taxable company. Another trigger: manufacturing, leasing, or servicing medical equipment from a Samoan physical establishment without a business license and without charging Samoan VAT/service export tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retrospective revocation of tax exemption; assessment of corporate income tax at the headline rate of 27% (or the applicable Samoan corporate rate) on all income from the date of first domestic activity; imposition of 20% late-payment interest; compounded penalties up to 200% of tax under-assessed; monetary penalty of WST 50,000 for unlicensed trading; a daily penalty of WST 1,000 until the offense ceases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners, and shadow directors become jointly and severally liable for all corporate tax arrears, penalties, and interest where the company's exemption is voided. Courts may pierce the corporate veil and seize personal assets. Directors of a void exempt IC may also be subject to travel bans under Samoa's Revenue Administration Act 2015 if tax debts exceed WST 25,000, and imprisonment for up to 5 years for willful tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a passive IC with no physical office, no Samoan-resident officer, no accounting records, and no genuine activity while claiming tax-exempt status and accepting third-party payments from medical device users; or holding the majority of profits from color Doppler ultrasound console intellectual property on behalf of a non-resident affiliate without any functions performed, assets used, or risks borne in Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Amendment Act, the Registrar may impose an economic substance penalty of WST 100,000 for the current year and WST 50,000,000 for repeated violations (in exceptional cases). The company may be struck off the international register and automatically converted to a domestic company. The Samoa Ministry of Revenue may also notify the OECD Global Forum, leading to adverse tax transparency ratings and automatic exchange of information (CRS/FATCA) disclosures to the shareholder's home jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and ultimate beneficial owners each face personal monetary fines of up to WST 150,000 and disqualification from holding directorship of any Samoa company for 10 years. The court may order the payment of all compliance costs and restitution of hidden profits. Where false declarations are made to the Registrar in respect of economic substance, directors are liable to imprisonment up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the International Company as an 'offshore payment conduit' in the export of medical imaging consoles: accepting third-party payments from a UBO who is a politically exposed person or sanctioned country without conducting KYC/CDD; structuring wire-transfers (Swift LC/TT) to avoid transaction reporting; or failing to maintain beneficial ownership records despite the low-risk AML tier (Banking_AML_Risk_Tier = Low_Risk_Standard).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2021, a body corporate may be fined up to WST 2,000,000 for a first offense and WST 5,000,000 for a subsequent offense. The FIU (Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit) may freeze bank accounts, patient hospitals paying the IC, and associated funds. The IC also faces civil forfeiture of all assets valued in connection with the offending transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual directors and compliance officers are personally liable for fines up to WST 500,000 and imprisonment not exceeding 10 years for willful failure to report suspicious transactions. Travel bans and extradition agreements with foreign States (including China, USA, Australia, New Zealand) apply where the medical-imaging export proceeds are alleged to be tainted. Directors cannot rely on the corporate veil or overseas residency to escape prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Trading While Struck Off / Non-registration Annual Renewal
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to operate the color Doppler ultrasound console export business after the IC license has been struck off for non-filing of the Annual Return or non-payment of the government fee; or signing contracts, issuing invoices, and receiving wire transfers in the name of a dissolved International Company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Trading with a struck-off company is an offense under the International Companies Act 1987. The company's agent, directors, and any person who physically trades in the name of the struck-off company commits an offense punishable by a fine of WST 30,000 plus repayment of all fees. Contracts entered into are voidable at the counterparty's option, making all LC/TT proceeds restitutable to the payer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Every director at the date of striking-off is personally liable for all debts and liabilities of the company incurred after the date of striking-off. The Samoan High Court may order restitution, award exemplary damages, and issue a director disqualification order for up to 12 years. Non-resident directors are still subject to personal jurisdiction via the registered agent and can be served internationally; their assets in any DTA or ECT treaty country may be enforced.
